study_design: Ecological cross-country correlation study of food consumption and cancer incidence, with a separate two-generation rat experiment
reason: The human analysis correlates country-level milk consumption with overall prostatic cancer incidence. It does not analyze aggressive, advanced, metastatic, high-grade, high-risk, or lethal incident prostate cancer.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Among the food items examined, milk was most closely correlated (r = 0.711) with prostatic cancer incidence, followed by meat and coffee.
estimate_classifications.reason: This is a country-level association with overall prostatic cancer incidence, without an aggressive disease definition.
